requirement:
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
**Obligation.** The only MUST is that, when authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration is included in the mandatory input set defined by `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.

**Implementation.** `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs) carries it out and has the `{impl}` reference.
- It starts `selectors` with `InputSelector::Requirements { requirements: subject_name }`. That selector is the first entry in the set, so it cannot be dropped as a duplicate.
- Each selector is turned into an input by `source_input`. For this selector, `resolve` plus `to_model_input` produce the declaration's `raw_lines`, the opening fence, body and closing fence.
- The test `requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines` in src/evidence.rs shows that `raw_lines` is `[":::{req} ready", "Ready MUST hold.", ":::"]`, and that `:impl:` and `:test:` option lines are not part of the text. The anchored files they name are contributed as separate inputs instead. I read "complete fenced declaration" as including the fence lines and the full body. It is not worded to require the option lines, and the project's own `requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` uses the same "complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines" wording over the same lines.
- Generated-evidence omission applies only to outline selectors (`generated_evidence_selector` returns false for `Requirements`), so the subject declaration is never omitted.

**Tests.** Each test below carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring_input`.
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` asserts the example subject's input `requirements == "requirements.case"` is present and `mandatory_inputs()[0]` is the subject. It also checks that cited declarations are added and that earlier evidence inputs are not carried forward.
- `unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment` asserts that `mandatory_inputs()` equals exactly `{requirements, matches, text: [":::{req} ready", "The project MUST be ready.", ":::"]}`, which is the complete fenced declaration.
- `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs` asserts the declaration comes first, with its fence lines, followed by the anchored file inputs.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` covers the failure path when the declaration is not available.

**Marking.** I found no implementing code without a reference and no unmarked tests. Behavior beyond the obligation, such as citation and site preparation, belongs to other requirements.

No gaps.

text: :::{req} authoring_input
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
